headline: Figma's Agent Era Is Here
subheadline: Figma's May release notes are all about co-designing with AI agents and MCP workflows — directly relevant to what you're building. Plus, Claude just shipped managed agents with MCP tunnels.

sections.label: Watch
sections.title: Figma Release Notes 2026: May Edition — Agents, MCP, and Vibe-Coded Prototypes
sections.description: This month's release notes are essentially a playbook for what you're building. They cover defining agents and MCP servers, taking vibe-coded prototypes further in Figma, and connecting design systems to code. The demo lab section starting at ~2 min looks especially relevant for your white-label sport apps system.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Figma AI in 2026: Everything It Can Do — and What It Still Can't
sections.description: A clear-eyed breakdown of where Figma AI actually is right now — including Dev Mode, Code Connect, MCP server, and Figma Make. The framing that Figma is evolving from a design tool into an AI-assisted product design platform is worth sitting with. Good calibration for what to lean into vs. what's still half-baked.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Claude Ships Managed Agents with Self-Hosted Sandboxes and MCP Tunnels
sections.description: This is a big one for your MCP work. Claude now supports managed agents that can run in self-hosted sandboxes with MCP tunnels — meaning teams get more control over execution and private network access. This could change how you architect the Claude ↔ Figma MCP integration for your company's design system. Worth digging into the specifics.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: The Future of Enterprise Design Systems: Agentic AI in 2026
sections.description: Supernova lays out how design systems are evolving from passive documentation into agentic workflows — automating token sync, component governance, and cross-platform consistency. Given you're building exactly this kind of system for white-label sport apps, their practical roadmap might validate (or challenge) your approach.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: AI in Design Systems: What's Actually Changing in 2026
sections.description: Zeroheight's take on the AI + design systems intersection, with specifics on token management and GitHub integration workflows. Less hype, more grounded in what design ops teams are actually adopting. Good companion read to the Supernova piece — different angle, same territory you're working in.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: MCP Tunnels — Private Network Access for AI Agents
sections.description: An MCP tunnel lets an AI agent securely access tools and data behind your company's private network — without exposing anything to the public internet. Think of it as a secure hallway between Claude and your internal Figma design system, where the agent can read and write but outsiders can't peek in. This is what makes enterprise MCP integrations viable rather than just cool demos.

sections.label: Did you know
sections.title: Cursor hit $2B annualized revenue in just 24 months
sections.description: For context, Slack took 7 years to reach its first billion. The AI-native IDE market isn't a niche anymore — it's mainstream developer infrastructure. Validates the bet you've made on vibe-coding as a real skill set, not a fad.

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: If Figma is becoming an AI-assisted product design platform, what does 'senior product designer' mean in 18 months?
sections.description: Figma's shift from design tool to product platform, Claude's managed agents, your own MCP integration work — you're already operating at the intersection of design leadership and product building. When you return from leave, the role that fits might not have the same title you left with. That could be a very good thing.
